bib.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift

legacy_report:
SOURCE: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift, Sergey Ioffe and Christian Szegedy (Google). Preprint as printed: arXiv:1502.03167v3, 2 Mar 2015. The PDF prints no venue, so the notes' "ICML 2015" cannot be confirmed from it.

COVERAGE: 45,461 of 45,461 chars, all 11 pages. References were read in full. Nothing skipped.

CLAIMS

Quotes are verbatim, except that line breaks are normalised to spaces. PDF hyphen-breaks are kept. All were checked by script against the extraction.

- claim: BN plus a bundle of training changes reaches the baseline's accuracy in 14x fewer steps.
  number: 14x (2.1M vs 31.0M steps to 72.2%)
  setup: ImageNet LSVRC2012, single-crop top-1 validation, authors' own Inception variant (13.6M params), batch 32, momentum SGD, distributed. BN-x5 = BN + LR x5 + no Dropout + L2 /5 + LR decay 6x faster + no LRN + more shuffling + fewer distortions.
  quote: "BN-x5 needs 14 times fewer steps than In- ception to reach the 72.2% accuracy"; "BN-x5 2.1· 106 73.0%"; "Inception 31.0· 106 72.2%"
  where: p7
- claim: BN alone, with no other changes, gives only a bit over 2x.
  number: 13.3M vs 31.0M steps; max 72.7%
  setup: BN-Baseline, same LR as Inception
  quote: "we match the accuracy of Inception in less than half the num- ber of training steps"; "BN-Baseline 13.3· 106 72.7%"
  where: p7
- claim: Adding BN alone does not capture the benefit; the other changes are needed.
  number: none
  setup: Sec 4.2.1
  quote: "Simply adding Batch Normalization to a network does not take full advantage of our method"
  where: p6
- claim: A 30x learning rate trains slower at first but ends higher.
  number: 74.8% at 6M steps; 72.2% at 2.7M
  setup: BN-x30, initial LR 0.045
  quote: "It reaches 74.8% after6·106 steps"; "BN-x30 2.7· 106 74.8%"
  where: p7
- claim: The x5 learning rate diverges without BN.
  number: 0.0075
  setup: original Inception
  quote: "The initial learning rate was increased by a factor of 5, to 0.0075. The same learning rate increase with original Inception caused the model pa- rameters to reach machine inﬁnity"
  where: p7
- claim: BN makes a deep sigmoid network trainable.
  number: 69.8% vs 1/1000
  setup: BN-x5-Sigmoid vs Inception with sigmoid
  quote: "BN-x5-Sigmoid 69.8%"; "Without Batch Normalization, Inception with sig- moid never achieves better than 1/1000 accuracy"
  where: p7
- claim: The record result is a 6-network, multicrop ensemble; a single model on a single crop is much weaker.
  number: 4.9% val, 4.82% test (ensemble); 5.82% (one model, 144 crops); 7.82% (single crop)
  setup: 224 resolution, 144 crops, 6 BN-x30 variants, some with Dropout at 5% or 10%; 50,000 val images, 100,000 test images
  quote: "BN-Inception ensemble 224 144 6 20.1% 4.9%*"; "BN-Inception multicrop 224 144 1 21.99% 5.82%"; "BN-Inception single crop 224 1 1 25.2% 7.82%"; "has reached 4.82% top-5 error on the 100000 images of the test set"
  where: p8
- claim: The nearest prior result was close, on the same test server.
  number: 4.94% vs 4.82%
  setup: He et al. 2015 ensemble, ILSVRC server
  quote: "The latter reports the top-5 error of 4.94%"
  where: p7
- claim: Better shuffling helped, which the authors read as consistent with BN regularising.
  number: about 1%
  setup: within-shard shuffling, one of the BN-x changes
  quote: "This led to about 1% improvements in the val- idation accuracy"
  where: p6
- claim: Dropout can be removed or weakened, and L2 reduced.
  number: L2 /5
  setup: Modified BN-Inception; no isolated measurement of the regularising effect
  quote: "in a batch-normalized network we found that it can be either removed or reduced in strength"; "the weight of this loss is reduced by a factor of 5"
  where: p5, p6
- claim: BN helped on a small MNIST sigmoid network, and one activation's distribution was more stable.
  number: 3 layers of 100; 50,000 steps; batch 60
  setup: MNIST, sigmoid, small Gaussian init; authors say it is not a state-of-the-art architecture
  quote: "3 fully-connected hidden layers with 100 activations each"; "We trained the network for 50000 steps, with 60 examples per mini-batch"; "for one typical activation from the last hidden layer of each network"
  where: p6
- claim: Inference uses population statistics from training mini-batches on the finished network, with an unbiased variance correction. Moving averages are presented as the alternative for tracking accuracy during training.
  number: Var[x] = m/(m-1) E_B[σ²_B]
  setup: Sec 3.1, Alg 2. Training variance in Alg 1 is 1/m.
  quote: "using the population, rather than mini-batch, statistics"; "Var[x] = mm−1· EB[σ2B]"; "Using moving averages in- stead, we can track the accuracy of a model as it trains"
  where: p4
- claim: Convolutional BN normalises per feature map, across batch and spatial locations.
  number: m' = m·pq
  setup: one γ, β pair per feature map
  quote: "we use the effec- tive mini-batch of size m′ =|B| = m· p q"
  where: p5
- claim: Mechanics: BN goes immediately before the nonlinearity, makes the bias redundant, needs m > 1, and adds two parameters per activation.
  number: 2; m > 1
  setup: Secs 3.1, 3.2, 5
  quote: "We add the BN transform immediately before the nonlinearity"; "Stochastic Gradient Descent with a mini-batch size m > 1"; "Batch Normalization adds only two extra parameters per activation"
  where: p5, p4, p8
- claim: The Jacobian account of why BN helps is explicitly a conjecture.
  number: singular values near 1
  setup: assumes Gaussian, uncorrelated, linear
  quote: "We further conjecture that Batch Normalization may lead the layer Jacobians to have singular values close to 1"; "the normalized values are not guaranteed to be Gaussian nor independent"
  where: p5

LIMITS
- Every speedup is in training steps. No wall-clock time or per-step BN overhead is reported.
- The text mentions no repeated runs, seeds or error bars, including for Fig 3.
- The 14x comparison is confounded: seven changes move together and there is no ablation.
- The baseline is the authors' own Inception variant, not published GoogLeNet.
- Evidence for reduced internal covariate shift (ICS) is one "typical" activation on MNIST. ICS was never measured on ImageNet, yet p7 says "We also veriﬁed that the reduction in internal covari- ate shift allows deep networks". The paper also hedges with "takes a step towards re- ducing internal covariate shift" (p2).
- Authors concede: "The precise effect of Batch Normaliza- tion on gradient propagation remains an area of further study" (p5).
- No experiment varies initialisation in a controlled way. "Less careful" rests on the Sec 3.3 scale argument and a sensitivity remark; the only initialisation change is "increased initial weights" in some ensemble members.
- Not tested: RNNs and domain adaptation (future work), small-batch behaviour, and non-vision tasks other than MNIST and ImageNet.
- Dated: the "best published" 4.9% claim. "Exceeding human raters" is against an estimate from Russakovsky et al. 2014.

BUILDS ON
- Whitening and input normalisation: LeCun et al., 1998b; Wiesler & Ney, 2011.
- Covariate shift: Shimodaira, 2000.
- Domain adaptation: Jiang, 2008.
- Activation-dependent optimisation or reparameterisation: Wiesler et al., 2014; Raiko et al., 2012; Povey et al., 2014; Desjardins & Kavukcuoglu (unpublished).
- Per-example normalisation: Lyu & Simoncelli, 2008.
- Closest prior layer: Gülçehre & Bengio, 2013.
- Base model: Szegedy et al., 2014.
- Regulariser it displaces: Srivastava et al., 2014.
- Jacobian argument: Saxe et al., 2013.

CODE: none in the paper. Worth keeping are Alg 1 (p3) and Alg 2 (p4), though their extraction is noisy, so copy from the page rather than the text.

FIGURES
- Fig 1, p6: MNIST test accuracy, and 15/50/85th percentile sigmoid inputs with and without BN. Shows the stability claim, and how narrow its evidence is.
- Fig 2, p7: validation accuracy vs steps for all variants. Shows the x5 and x30 trade-off faster than prose.
- Fig 3, p7: table of steps to 72.2% and max accuracy. Separates BN alone from the full bundle at a glance.
- Fig 4, p8: table of single-crop, multicrop and ensemble results. Prevents reading 4.9% as a single-model figure.
- Fig 5, p11: architecture table. Reference only.

COMPARISON WITH NOTES

Grep of 1502.03167 finds four files:
- `data-science/02-deep-learning/notes/02-optimisation-and-regularisation.md` (cited at line 128, frontmatter line 15)
- `data-science/02-deep-learning/references.md` line 30
- `generative-ai/09-llms-from-scratch/notes/02-makemore.md` (frontmatter line 5; prose at line 293 via PDF link)
- `generative-ai/09-llms-from-scratch/references.md` line 26

There are no hits under `programming/`, which only has an unrelated "BN" match. I also checked both pillars' decks and uncited mentions.

Mismatches

1. Optimisation note line 128, "reached the same accuracy on a state-of-the-art ImageNet model in 14× fewer steps". It follows the abstract, but credits BN with what the bundle did. BN alone was under 2.33x (13.3M vs 31.0M). Missing setup: BN-x5 with the Sec 4.2.1 changes, 72.2% single-crop top-1 validation, steps only.
2. Makemore note line 284, "unit Gaussian *by construction*". The paper fixes only mean and variance, and states the values are "not guaranteed to be Gaussian". This is a factual overstatement for the cited method. It may come from the lecture.
3. Makemore note line 280 and deck `generative-ai/09-llms-from-scratch/slides/deck.yaml` line 226 and notes at line 229, "BatchNorm adds nothing until the model gets deep" / "BatchNorm matters for depth". This generalises from a one-hidden-layer tanh MLP with init already fixed. The paper's smallest test, 3 sigmoid layers of 100 on MNIST with small Gaussian init, did benefit. Paper-backed scope would be "on this already well-initialised shallow net". Note line 280 is closer to this than the deck takeaway.

Under-qualified

4. Line 128, "4.9% top-5 validation error": lacks 6 networks and 144 crops. Single-crop single-model was 7.82%, and test error was 4.82%. "Ensemble" alone does not convey the crops.
5. Line 128, "showed it allows... less careful initialisation": too strong, as no experiment isolates it. High learning rates are shown (x5 diverges without BN, x30 trains with it), though on one architecture.
6. Line 128, "regularises somewhat": supported only through confounded changes, and the ensemble still used light Dropout in some members. Acceptable if worded as "the authors found".
7. Line 128, "The paper's explanation, reduced internal covariate shift": the paper also offers scale invariance (Sec 3.3) and a flagged Jacobian conjecture, so it does not give a single explanation.
8. Deck `data-science/02-deep-learning/slides/deck.yaml` line 153 notes, "speeds up training a great deal": no setup and no steps-only caveat.

Uncited claims

9. Line 128, "is disputed, and the practical benefits are not", and makemore line 293, "an explanation later work disputes". Neither names a source, and this paper cannot support them. Grep finds no "santurkar" or 1805.11604 in the four pillars searched (data-science, generative-ai, programming, ai-engineering), and the ledger has no 1805.11604 row. "Are not" disputed is a universal claim with nothing behind it. I have read nothing that supports or refutes the dispute.

Lesser points

10. Test statistics: line 128 is correct. Line 130 and makemore lines 295 and 696 ("every BatchNorm layer stores running statistics") present the EMA as the default and calibration as the later fix. Alg 2 is itself a post-training average over mini-batches, with moving averages as the alternative. That is framework practice, not the paper; the notes do not misattribute it, but the framing hides a useful point.
11. Variance: the paper uses 1/m in training (Alg 1) and an m/(m-1) correction at inference. Makemore's code uses unbiased `.var`/`.std` in training, and lines 443 and 696 use n-1. So the `nan` at batch 1 (line 696) comes from that implementation. Under Alg 1 the variance would be 0 and ε would prevent the division by zero, though the paper does require m > 1.
12. Makemore line 293 cites this paper by PDF link only, unlike the `(arXiv:..., Author, venue)` form used elsewhere.
13. Ledger line 438: `"status": "queued"` although two notes cite the paper, and `"note"` points to `01-neural-networks-fundamentals.md`, which does not cite it (the citing note is 02). Its `"topic"` and `"pillar"` are `classical-ml`, while the citing notes are in deep learning and LLMs from scratch.
14. Makemore frontmatter lists 2105.07576 twice (lines 4 and 8 of the sources block).
15. `data-science/02-deep-learning/README.md` line 56, "cost 9 points", omits its setup (digits, batch 32). This is a local run, not the paper.

Confirmed correct
- Line 128: learned γ, β and identity representation; population statistics at test.
- Makemore table: regulariser via batch jitter; bias redundant (`bias=False`); placement after the linear layer.
- Both references rows.

Unused support the caller may want
- 69.8% vs 1/1000 on sigmoid fits makemore's tanh saturation story.
- Sec 3.2 (m' = m·pq) is the principle behind the makemore 3-d fix at line 557, reducing over (0, 1).

PROBLEMS
- Extraction leaves math broken (e.g. "31.0· 106" means 31.0·10^6, "mm−1" means m/(m-1)) and splits words at line ends. Figure 1 and 2 plots are not text; I read their captions and the axis labels that extracted, not the rendered curves. Stated results come from the prose and Fig 3.
- pypdf prints fontTools warnings, which are harmless.
- The first 40,000-char read was followed by a second range to the end.
- No embedded instructions.
